q: How do you say 'water' in Japanese?
explain: 水 (みず, mizu) means water, especially cool or cold water.
hook: Mizu sounds like 'misty' - think of a water mist.

sources.title: mizu - Jisho.org
sources.quote: Noun 1. water (esp. cool or cold)

sources.title: 水 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary
sources.quote: 水 ( みず ) ( mizu )

q: How do you say 'cooked rice' in Japanese?
explain: ご飯 (ごはん, gohan) means cooked rice, and it can also mean a meal.
hook: Go-han: 'go have a handful' of rice.

sources.title: gohan - Jisho.org
sources.quote: Noun 1. cooked rice ... Noun 2. meal ... Other forms 御飯 【ごはん】

sources.title: ご飯 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary
sources.quote: 【 御飯 ごはん 】 [noun] cooked rice [noun] a meal of any sort

q: How do you say 'delicious' in Japanese?
explain: おいしい (oishii) is an i-adjective meaning good-tasting, delicious or tasty; it is usually written in kana alone.
hook: Oh-ee-shee: 'Oh, he's eating!' because it's tasty.

sources.title: 美味しい - Jisho.org
sources.quote: I-adjective (keiyoushi) 1. good(-tasting); nice; delicious; tasty Usually written using kana alone

sources.title: 美味しい - Wiktionary, the free dictionary
sources.quote: 美味 ( おい ) しい ( oishii ) -i

q: What is the polite Japanese word for the bill or check at a restaurant?
explain: お会計 (おかいけい, okaikei) is a polite word for the bill or check at a restaurant.

sources.title: お会計 - Jisho.org
sources.quote: かい けい お 会計 Common word ... Noun 1. bill (at a restaurant); check Polite (teineigo) language

q: Which Japanese expression means 'thank you (for the meal just served)', said as you begin eating?
explain: いただきます (itadakimasu) is glossed as 'thank you (for the meal just served); I receive (this meal)' and is usually written in kana.
hook: Itadaki-masu: 'I take it, thanks' before the first bite.

sources.title: itadakimasu - Jisho.org
sources.quote: Expressions (phrases, clauses, etc.) 1. thank you (for the meal just served); I receive (this meal) Usually written using kana alone

sources.title: 頂きます - Jisho.org
sources.quote: いただ 頂 き ま す Common word JLPT N3

q: Which polite Japanese expression means 'thank you for the meal' after you have finished eating?
explain: ごちそうさまでした is glossed 'thank you for the meal; that was a delicious meal; what a wonderful meal' and is usually written in kana.
hook: Go-chiso: 'go cheese-o' - the feast is done.

sources.title: gochisousamadeshita - Jisho.org
sources.quote: Expressions (phrases, clauses, etc.) 1. thank you for the meal; that was a delicious meal; what a wonderful meal Polite (teineigo) language , Usually written using kana alone Other forms ご馳走さまでした 【ごちそうさまでした】 、 御馳走様でした 【ごちそうさまでした】
